etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English outright, equivalent to out +‎ right.

quote.citation: 1951 April, R. S. McNaught, “Railway Enthusiasts”, in Railway Magazine, number 600, page 269:
quote.text: Special facilities frequently are provided to enable visiting photographers to get the best results, whereas in the past cameras were sometimes banned outright.

definitions.definition: (sports) To release a player outright, without conditions.

quote.citation: 2007 August 30, Ben Shpigel, “Martínez to Audition for Mets’ Brain Trust”, in New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Sandy Alomar Jr. cleared waivers and was outrighted to Class AA Binghamton in preparation for his promotion when rosters expand Saturday.
